answers.answer: Fix a point as the centre and mark points at the same distance from it all the way round.
solution: A circle is the set of points at a constant distance from a fixed point (definition-1).
Fix a peg at the centre spot of the field.
Tie a rope to the peg. Its length is the radius.
Keep the rope tight and walk round the peg, marking the ground at each step.
The marked points are all the same distance from the centre, so they form the circle.

answers.answer: I can save water by using only the amount I need and not wasting it.
solution: This is an open question, so there is no single fixed answer.
Close the tap while brushing teeth or washing hands.
Repair leaking taps and pipes.
Do not waste water when washing cars or watering plants.
Tell family and friends to save water too.

answers.answer: Infinite (unlimited) number of diameters
solution: A diameter is a chord passing through the centre (definition-6).
Infinitely many straight lines pass through the centre.
Each of these lines gives a diameter.
So a circle has an infinite number of diameters.

answers.answer: AC; BM; AC; AC. So AM + MC > AC, AM + BM > AC, AB > AC.
solution: In triangle AMC, the sum of two sides is greater than the third side: AM + MC > AC.
CM = BM (radii), so replace MC by BM.
Thus AM + BM > AC.
AM + BM = AB because M lies on AB.
So AB > AC, and the blanks are AC, BM, AC, AC.

answers.answer: diameter = 2r, perimeter = 2πr, area = πr²
solution: The diameter passes through the centre and is made of two radii, so it is r + r = 2r.
The perimeter of a circle is 2πr.
The area of a circle is πr².

answers.answer: A circle M drawn with compasses on transparent paper.
solution: Put the compass point on a point M and mark it as the centre.
Open the compass to any radius.
Turn the compass in one full turn on the transparent paper.
This gives circle M.

answers.answer: A straight line L1 through M, cutting the circle into two arcs.
solution: Place a ruler so that its edge passes through the centre M.
Draw the straight line L1 across the whole circle.
L1 meets the circle at two points and divides it into two arcs.

answers.answer: The two parts of the circle on either side of L1 coincide exactly.
solution: Fold the paper along L1.
One part of the circle falls exactly on the other part.
So L1 is an axis of symmetry of the circle.

answers.answer: In every case the two parts coincide, so every line through the centre is an axis of symmetry.
solution: Draw L2, L3, L4, ... each passing through M.
Fold the paper along each line in turn.
Each time the two parts of the circle coincide exactly.
So any straight line through the centre is an axis of symmetry of the circle.

answers.answer: Infinite (unlimited) number of axes of symmetry
solution: Any straight line passing through the centre is an axis of symmetry (rule-5).
Infinitely many lines pass through the centre.
So the circle has an infinite number of axes of symmetry.

answers.answer: 2 cm or 14 cm. Yes, there is another answer.
solution: Draw the line through M perpendicular to both chords. It bisects each chord (rule-7).
For AB = 12: half is 6 cm. The distance from M is √(10² − 6²) = √64 = 8 cm.
For CD = 16: half is 8 cm. The distance from M is √(10² − 8²) = √36 = 6 cm.
If the chords are on the same side of M, the distance between them is 8 − 6 = 2 cm.
If the chords are on opposite sides of M, the distance is 8 + 6 = 14 cm.
Both positions are possible, so the answer is 2 cm or 14 cm.

answers.answer: The longer chord AB is closer to the centre.
solution: The perpendicular from M to a chord bisects it (rule-7).
A longer chord has a longer half-chord.
The distance from M to the chord is √(r² − (half chord)²).
A longer half-chord makes this distance smaller.
So AB, the longer chord, is closer to the centre.

answers.answer: segment DC
solution: The surface of the circle is the circle together with its inside points.
The line AB is inside the surface only between D and C.
Answer: the line segment DC.

answers.answer: the set of points inside the circle (the surface of circle M)
solution: M is the centre, so it is not on the circle.
The centre is inside the circle.
Answer: M ∈ the set of points inside the circle, so it also lies on the surface of circle M.

answers.answer: NC > NA, because NC + MC > MN and MC = MA.
solution: Draw the radius MC. In triangle NMC the sum of two sides is greater than the third side: NC + MC > MN.
MC = MA (radii).
So NC + MA > MN.
A lies on MN, so MN = MA + NA.
So NC + MA > MA + NA.
Subtract MA from both sides: NC > NA (Q.E.D.).

answers.answer: The straight line through the centre and the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to that chord.
solution: In figure 1, line L passes through the centre M and C, the midpoint of chord BA.
L is perpendicular to chord BA.
So the straight line through the centre and the midpoint of any chord is perpendicular to the chord.

answers.answer: The straight line through the centre and perpendicular to a chord bisects that chord.
solution: In figure 2, line L passes through the centre M and is perpendicular to chord BA at C.
Then BC = CA.
So the straight line through the centre perpendicular to a chord bisects the chord.

answers.answer: The perpendicular bisector of any chord of a circle passes through the centre of the circle.

L also passes through the centre M.
